question.text: A 'key person' (key man) clause in AIF documentation typically provides that:

answer.text: All investors must be high-net-worth individuals
If one or more specified key persons are not available to devote the necessary time to the investment, the AIF / management company is prohibited from making new investments
The fund manager cannot hire new employees
All investments must be personally approved by SEBI

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.173-174) describes the key man clause as a provision that prohibits the AIF / management company from making new investments if one or more specified key persons are not available to devote the necessary time to the investment activities of the fund. The clause protects investors by ensuring that capital is not deployed when the key individuals they relied upon are not actively committed to the fund. The Trap: The key man clause does not impose investor eligibility rules, does not stop the manager from hiring staff, and does not require SEBI to personally approve investments. It is specifically a "no new investments" trigger tied to the availability of the named key persons. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.173-174 (key man clause — prohibition on new investments if key persons are not available to devote necessary time to the investment).
